answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a triple-resource spiral: each epoch, every identity must prove compute, storage, and bandwidth together, in a mix that spirals to a new corner of the ridge each time, like a nebula shifting shape. A farm renting a thousand identical servers fails when the mix turns storage-heavy, because faking all three at once per fake costs real hardware and pipes. One honest agent, already running a single node, passes the cheap sampled checks once.
